records.source: הֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Give thanks to YHWH, for [he is] good, for to forever [is] his loyal love.
pieces: Give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever.

L.1: Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] good, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever.

R.1: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good! His faithful love lasts forever.

decisions.choice: Book Five of the Psalms begins
decisions.reason: The Psalms are gathered into five books. Book Four closed with the blessing of 106:48; Book Five (Psalms 107-150) opens here and ends with the praise of Psalm 150. The psalm has no title.

decisions.choice: the song of the temple: good, love forever
decisions.reason: "He is good; his loyal love is forever" is the temple's great song of thanks (100:5; 106:1; 118:1; 136:1; 1 Chronicles 16:34; 2 Chronicles 5:13). Psalm 106 begins with the same words, and Psalm 107 answers its closing prayer to be gathered from the nations (106:47) with the gathering of verse 3.
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: for ... for: two reasons for thanks
decisions.reason: Both lines begin with the same word (ki): the LORD is good, and his love lasts.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.heading: Let the rescued give thanks

records.source: יֹ֭אמְרוּ גְּאוּלֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר גְּ֝אָלָ֗ם מִיַּד־צָֽר׃
records.gloss: Let [the] redeemed of YHWH say [so], whom he has redeemed from [the] hand of [the] foe,
pieces: Let those whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has bought back say it, those {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} freed from the grip of the enemy,

L.2: Let the redeemed of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say [so], whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has redeemed from [the] hand of [the] foe,

R.2: All the people whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has set free should say it! He rescued them from the power of their enemies.

decisions.reason: The verb (ga'al) is what a near relative did in buying back family land or a relative sold as a slave (Leviticus 25:25, 48). God redeemed Israel from Egypt (Exodus 6:6) and from exile (Isaiah 43:1); "the redeemed of the LORD" are his people brought home (Isaiah 62:12).

decisions.choice: say so: say the words of verse 1
decisions.reason: What the redeemed are to say is the song of verse 1, "his loyal love is forever".

decisions.choice: the hand of the foe: the enemy's power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control (31:16).

decisions.choice: those whom the LORD has bought back
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of buying back (m1) in everyday words.

records.source: וּֽמֵאֲרָצ֗וֹת קִ֫בְּצָ֥ם מִמִּזְרָ֥ח וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֑ב מִצָּפ֥וֹן וּמִיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: and from [the] lands he has gathered them, from east and from west, from north and from [the] sea.
pieces: and brought them in from other lands, from the east and the west, the north and the south.

L.3: and from the lands {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has gathered them, from east and from west, from north and from [the] sea.

R.3: He gathered them from far-off countries, from the east, the west, the north and the south.

decisions.choice: gathered from the lands: the return from exile
decisions.reason: God had promised to gather his scattered people from every direction (Deuteronomy 30:3-4; Isaiah 43:5-6). The psalm thanks him for bringing them home.

alternatives: the south (reading yamin, a word very like it)
decisions.reason: "The sea" usually means the west, but the west is already named. Here it probably means the south, perhaps the Red Sea; one small change of letters gives the word for "south".
Balanced and Readable give the direction that completes the four (m2); Literal keeps "sea".

decisions.choice: brought them in (B); He gathered them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced continues the sentence of verse 2; Readable begins a new sentence and names who gathered them.

records.source: תָּע֣וּ בַ֭מִּדְבָּר בִּישִׁימ֣וֹן דָּ֑רֶךְ עִ֥יר מ֝וֹשָׁ֗ב לֹ֣א מָצָֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: They wandered in the wilderness, in a wasteland [of a] way; a city of dwelling not they found.
pieces: Some strayed through the wilderness, along a barren track, and found no town to live in.

L.4: They wandered in the wilderness, on a desolate way; a city [to] dwell [in] they did not find.

R.4: Some people were lost in the desert. They traveled through empty land and could not find any town to live in.

decisions.choice: four pictures of people in trouble
decisions.reason: The psalm draws four groups who cried to the LORD and were rescued: travelers lost in the desert (4-9), prisoners (10-16), the sick (17-22) and sailors in a storm (23-32). They may be four kinds of people, or four pictures of Israel in exile and its return.

decisions.choice: a wasteland of a way: a desolate track
alternatives: in the wasteland they found no way to a city
decisions.reason: The words "in a wasteland, a way" are terse. They describe the road the travelers were on, or they belong with the next line: they found no way to a city.

decisions.choice: a city of dwelling: a place to settle
decisions.reason: A town with people in it, where travelers could find food, water and a home.
Balanced and Readable mark the start of the first group with "Some" (m1).

records.source: רְעֵבִ֥ים גַּם־צְמֵאִ֑ים נַ֝פְשָׁ֗ם בָּהֶ֥ם תִּתְעַטָּֽף׃
records.gloss: Hungry, also thirsty, their soul in them was fainting.
pieces: Starving and parched, they felt their life draining out of them.

L.5: Hungry, thirsty too, their soul was fainting within them.

R.5: They had no food and no water, and they were close to dying.

decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the self as a living, breathing being; for it to faint is to come near death.
The verb ('ataf) is used of a spirit growing faint in 77:4 and 142:4.

decisions.choice: their life draining out of them (B); close to dying (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m1).

records.source: וַיִּצְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם מִ֝מְּצֽוּקוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יַצִּילֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And they cried out to YHWH in the distress [that was] to them; from their troubles he delivered them.
pieces: In their distress they called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued them from their troubles.

L.6: Then they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in their distress; from their troubles {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delivered them.

R.6: In their trouble they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued them from their suffering.

decisions.reason: This line comes four times (verses 6, 13, 19, 28), once in each picture of people in trouble, and each time only the verb of rescue changes. Each time the second refrain follows two verses later (8, 15, 21, 31).
The verb (tsa'aq) is the cry of people in need, like Israel's cry in Egypt (Exodus 3:7).
The verb (natsal, causative) is to pull someone out of danger. Each refrain has its own verb: delivered (6), saved (13, 19), brought out (28).

decisions.choice: in their distress ... from their troubles
alternatives: they cried out ... in their trouble, and he ... them from their distress
decisions.reason: The refrain keeps the same wording each time; Balanced and Readable put "in their distress" first, where it is heard most.

records.source: וַ֭יַּֽדְרִיכֵם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יְשָׁרָ֑ה לָ֝לֶ֗כֶת אֶל־עִ֥יר מוֹשָֽׁב׃
records.gloss: And he led them by a straight way to go to a city of dwelling.
pieces: He guided them on a level road until they came to a town to live in.

L.7: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them by a straight way, to go to a city [to] dwell [in].

R.7: He led them straight to a town where they could make their homes.

decisions.reason: The word (yashar) means straight or level. It answers the wandering of verse 4: the lost are led by the shortest road to the town they could not find.
God led Israel through the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:2) and promised to lead the exiles home on a level road (Isaiah 40:3-4; Jeremiah 31:9).

records.source: יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: Let them give thanks to YHWH [for] his loyal love, and his wonders to [the] children of humankind.
pieces: Let them give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love and for the wonders {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} works for humankind.

L.8: Let them give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [for] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love, and [for] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders to the children of humankind.

R.8: They should thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love and for the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does for people.

decisions.reason: This verse comes four times, word for word (8, 15, 21, 31), after each rescue. Those who were rescued are called to give the thanks of verse 1.
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).
The word (nifla'ot) is used of God's acts in Egypt and the wilderness (78:4; 106:22).

decisions.choice: to the children of humankind: done for people
decisions.reason: The wonders are done for human beings, and are seen by them. "Children of humankind" (bene 'adam) means people in general.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: כִּי־הִ֭שְׂבִּיעַ נֶ֣פֶשׁ שֹׁקֵקָ֑ה וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ רְ֝עֵבָה מִלֵּא־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: For he has satisfied [the] longing soul, and [the] hungry soul he has filled [with] good.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives drink to those who are parched and fills the starving with good food.

L.9: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has satisfied the longing soul, and the hungry soul {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has filled [with] good.

R.9: He gives water to thirsty people, and good food to people who are hungry.

decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) can mean the throat and so the appetite; with "longing" and "hungry" it is the self that thirsts and hungers.
The word (shoqeqah) describes restless desire, here most likely thirst after the "thirsty" of verse 5 (Isaiah 29:8).
Mary's song takes up these words: "he has filled the hungry with good things" (Luke 1:53).

decisions.choice: those who are parched, the starving (B); thirsty people, people who are hungry (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak of the people themselves (m1).
Readable says what satisfying a thirsty soul means (m2).

records.source: יֹ֭שְׁבֵי חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָ֑וֶת אֲסִירֵ֖י עֳנִ֣י וּבַרְזֶֽל׃
records.gloss: Those who sat [in] darkness and deep darkness, prisoners of affliction and iron,
pieces: Some lived in darkness, in the blackest gloom, held fast in misery and iron,

L.10: Those who sat in darkness and deep darkness, prisoners [in] affliction and iron,

R.10: Some people were sitting in darkness, in the deepest gloom. They were prisoners, held in iron chains and in misery.

decisions.reason: The second group sits in a dark prison (verses 10-16). Exile was often pictured as prison (Isaiah 42:7; 49:9).
As in 23:4 (tsalmavet): deep, deadly darkness. The same words come again in verse 14.
The two words make one picture: the misery of being bound in iron (105:18).
As in verse 4, Balanced and Readable mark the start of a new group.
Readable says what the iron is.

records.source: כִּֽי־הִמְר֥וּ אִמְרֵי־אֵ֑ל וַעֲצַ֖ת עֶלְי֣וֹן נָאָֽצוּ׃
records.gloss: for they had rebelled against [the] words of God, and [the] counsel of [the] Most High they had spurned.
pieces: because they had defied what God said and scorned the purpose of the Most High.

L.11: for they had rebelled against the words of God, and the counsel of the Most High they had spurned.

R.11: This happened because they had turned against what God said. They had refused to listen to the advice of the God who is above all.

decisions.reason: Unlike the travelers, these prisoners brought their trouble on themselves by turning from God's word. Even so, when they cry out, he sets them free (verse 13).
The word ('etsah) is advice given, or the plan God has made (33:11).

decisions.choice: the Most High: God above all
decisions.reason: The title ('Elyon) names God as the highest over all (7:18; 46:5).

decisions.choice: the God who is above all
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title means.
Readable begins a new sentence and links it to verse 10.

records.source: וַיַּכְנַ֣ע בֶּעָמָ֣ל לִבָּ֑ם כָּ֝שְׁל֗וּ וְאֵ֣ין עֹזֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And he humbled with toil their heart; they stumbled, and there was no helper.
pieces: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke their pride with hard labor; they fell, and no one came to help.

L.12: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} humbled their heart with toil; they stumbled, and [there was] no one to help.

R.12: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} humbled them with hard work. They fell down, and no one helped them.

decisions.reason: The word ('amal) is hard work and the misery it brings, here the forced labor of prisoners.

decisions.choice: humbled their heart: brought down their pride
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner self; to bring it low is to break the pride that rebelled (verse 11).
Balanced says what the idiom means (m2).

records.source: וַיִּזְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם מִ֝מְּצֻֽקוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹשִׁיעֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And they cried out to YHWH in the distress [that was] to them; from their troubles he saved them.
pieces: In their distress they called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved them from their troubles.

L.13: Then they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in their distress; from their troubles {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved them.

R.13: In their trouble they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved them from their suffering.

decisions.reason: As in verse 6; only the verb of rescue changes.
As in verse 6.
The verb (yasha', causative) is the common word for saving and rescue; the same verb comes in verse 19.

decisions.choice: in their distress ... from their troubles
alternatives: they cried out ... in their trouble, and he ... them from their distress
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

records.source: יֽ֭וֹצִיאֵם מֵחֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָ֑וֶת וּמוֹסְר֖וֹתֵיהֶ֣ם יְנַתֵּֽק׃
records.gloss: He brought them out from darkness and deep darkness, and their bonds he tore apart.
pieces: He led them out of the darkness and the blackest gloom and snapped the chains that held them.

L.14: He brought them out of darkness and deep darkness, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tore apart their bonds.

R.14: He led them out of the darkness and the deep gloom. He broke their chains apart.

decisions.choice: darkness and deep darkness: the words of verse 10
decisions.reason: The rescue answers the trouble word for word: those who sat in darkness and deep darkness (verse 10) are brought out of it.
The word (moserot) is the bands that tie a prisoner or an animal (2:3).

records.source: יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: Let them give thanks to YHWH [for] his loyal love, and his wonders to [the] children of humankind.
pieces: Let them give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love and for the wonders {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} works for humankind.

L.15: Let them give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [for] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love, and [for] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders to the children of humankind.

R.15: They should thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love and for the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does for people.

decisions.reason: As in verse 8, word for word.
As in verse 1.
As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: to the children of humankind: done for people
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: כִּֽי־שִׁ֭בַּר דַּלְת֣וֹת נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וּבְרִיחֵ֖י בַרְזֶ֣ל גִּדֵּֽעַ׃
records.gloss: For he has broken gates of bronze, and bars of iron he has cut down.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} smashes doors of bronze and hacks through bars of iron.

L.16: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shattered gates of bronze, and bars of iron {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has cut through.

R.16: He can break down bronze gates and cut through iron bars.

decisions.choice: gates of bronze, bars of iron: Isaiah 45:2
decisions.reason: God promised Cyrus, who let the exiles go home, "I will break doors of bronze and cut through bars of iron" (Isaiah 45:2). The same words stand here.
As verse 9 follows the first call to thanks, this verse gives the reason for the second.

decisions.choice: smashes, hacks through (B); can break, cut (R)
decisions.reason: The verbs are past in form, but the verse says what God does; Balanced and Readable use the present, as in verse 9.

records.source: אֱ֭וִלִים מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ פִּשְׁעָ֑ם וּֽ֝מֵעֲוֺֽנֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יִתְעַנּֽוּ׃
records.gloss: Fools, because of [the] way of their transgression and because of their iniquities, were afflicted.
pieces: Some were fools, and their rebellious ways and their wrongdoing brought suffering on them.

L.17: Fools, because of the way of their rebellion and because of their iniquities, were afflicted.

R.17: Some people were foolish. Because they turned against God and did wrong, they became sick and suffered.

decisions.reason: The third group are sick and near death (verses 17-22): they cannot eat (18), and God heals them (20).

alternatives: the sick (with a small change of letters)
decisions.reason: The word ('evilim) means not a lack of brains but a stubborn refusal of God's ways (Proverbs 1:7). A small change of letters would give "sick", which fits the picture, but the Hebrew as it stands makes the folly the cause of the sickness.
The word (pesha') is a breaking away from God, a revolt (51:3).
As in verse 4, Balanced and Readable mark the start of a new group.
Readable names the suffering that verses 18 and 20 describe (m1).

records.source: כָּל־אֹ֭כֶל תְּתַעֵ֣ב נַפְשָׁ֑ם וַ֝יַּגִּ֗יעוּ עַד־שַׁ֥עֲרֵי מָֽוֶת׃
records.gloss: All food their soul loathed, and they reached to [the] gates of death.
pieces: They could not stand the sight of food, and came close to the gates of death.

L.18: All food their soul loathed, and they reached to the gates of death.

R.18: They could not eat anything at all, and they were about to die.

decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the self as it hungers (verse 9); here it turns away from food.

decisions.choice: the gates of death: the edge of the world of the dead
decisions.reason: Death is pictured as a city with gates (9:14). To reach them is to be about to die.

alternatives: they reached the gates of death
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

records.source: וַיִּזְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם מִ֝מְּצֻֽקוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹשִׁיעֵֽם׃

L.19: Then they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in their distress; from their troubles {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved them.

R.19: In their trouble they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved them from their suffering.

decisions.reason: As in verse 6; only the verb of rescue changes.
As in verse 6.
As in verse 13.

records.source: יִשְׁלַ֣ח דְּ֭בָרוֹ וְיִרְפָּאֵ֑ם וִֽ֝ימַלֵּ֗ט מִשְּׁחִיתוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: He sent his word and healed them, and delivered [them] from their pits.
pieces: He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word and made them well; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pulled them out of the pit of death.

L.20: He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word and healed them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delivered [them] from their pits.

R.20: He only had to speak, and they were healed. He kept them from dying.

decisions.choice: he sent his word: the word as God's messenger
decisions.reason: God's word goes out like a messenger and does what he sends it to do (147:15, 18; Isaiah 55:11). The centurion in the Gospels trusted Jesus in the same way: "only say the word" (Matthew 8:8).
The word (shechitot) is found only here and in Lamentations 4:20. It is probably a pit or trap, here the pit of death; it may mean "destruction".
Readable says what sending his word means (m1).

decisions.choice: the pit of death (B); kept them from dying (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the likely sense (m2).

decisions.choice: to the children of humankind: done for people
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: וְ֭יִזְבְּחוּ זִבְחֵ֣י תוֹדָ֑ה וִֽיסַפְּר֖וּ מַעֲשָׂ֣יו בְּרִנָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And let them sacrifice sacrifices of thanksgiving, and let them recount his works with a shout of joy.
pieces: Let them bring offerings of thanks and with glad shouts recount what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

L.22: And let them sacrifice sacrifices of thanksgiving, and let them recount {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works with shouts of joy.

R.22: Let them offer sacrifices to thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and shout for joy as they tell what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

decisions.choice: sacrifices of thanksgiving: the thank offering
decisions.reason: The thank offering (todah) was a sacrifice brought after a rescue, eaten with family and friends while the story was told (Leviticus 7:12-15; 50:14; 116:17).

decisions.choice: shout of joy: a ringing cry
decisions.reason: The word (rinnah) is a loud, glad cry, often in song (30:6).

records.source: יוֹרְדֵ֣י הַ֭יָּם בָּאֳנִיּ֑וֹת עֹשֵׂ֥י מְ֝לָאכָ֗ה בְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Those who went down [to] the sea in ships, doing business on many waters,
pieces: Some sailed out to sea in ships, trading over the vast waters,

L.23: Those who go down [to] the sea in ships, doing business on many waters,

R.23: Some people sailed the sea in ships. They were traders, carrying goods across the wide ocean.

decisions.choice: the fourth picture: sailors in a storm
decisions.reason: The last group are seafarers caught in a storm (verses 23-32). Israel was not a people of sailors, and the sea stood for chaos and danger (93:3-4); only God rules it (89:10).

decisions.choice: go down to the sea: put out to sea
decisions.reason: One goes down from the hills to the shore, and from the land onto the sea (Isaiah 42:10).
Verse 23 names the group and verse 24 says what they saw, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
As in verse 4, Balanced and Readable mark the start of a new group.

records.source: הֵ֣מָּה רָ֭אוּ מַעֲשֵׂ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו בִּמְצוּלָֽה׃
records.gloss: they, they saw [the] works of YHWH and his wonders in [the] deep.
pieces: they saw for themselves what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} marvels out on the deep.

L.24: they saw the works of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders in the deep.

R.24: They saw with their own eyes what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} can do, and the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does on the deep sea.

decisions.reason: The pronoun (hemmah) is stressed: it is these seafarers, of all people, who saw what God can do.

decisions.choice: the deep: the depths of the sea
decisions.reason: The word (metsulah) is the deep water where things sink (Exodus 15:5; 69:3).

decisions.choice: for themselves (B); with their own eyes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable carry the stress on "they" (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר וַֽ֭יַּעֲמֵד ר֣וּחַ סְעָרָ֑ה וַתְּרוֹמֵ֥ם גַּלָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he spoke and made stand a wind of storm, and it lifted up its waves.
pieces: At {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word a gale sprang up and drove the waves of the sea high.

L.25: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke and raised a storm wind, and it lifted high its waves.

R.25: He gave a command, and a strong wind began to blow. It made huge waves on the sea.

decisions.choice: he spoke: the storm comes at God's command
decisions.reason: The storm is not chance: God commands the wind (148:8). The one who raised it is the one who stills it (verse 29).
The verb ('amad, causative) is to set up or bring into being; the storm wind rises at his word.
"Its" refers to the sea of verse 23.

decisions.choice: of the sea (B); on the sea (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the sea (m3).

records.source: יַעֲל֣וּ שָׁ֭מַיִם יֵרְד֣וּ תְהוֹמ֑וֹת נַ֝פְשָׁ֗ם בְּרָעָ֥ה תִתְמוֹגָֽג׃
records.gloss: They went up [to the] heavens, they went down [to the] deeps; their soul in evil melted.
pieces: Up they were tossed to the sky, and down into the depths; in such danger their nerve gave way.

L.26: They went up [to the] heavens, they went down [to the] depths; their soul melted in [the] evil.

R.26: The sailors were thrown up toward the sky and down into the deep. They were so terrified that they lost all courage.

decisions.choice: up to the heavens, down to the deeps: huge waves
decisions.reason: The ship rides up waves that seem to reach the sky and falls into troughs that seem to reach the bottom of the sea.

decisions.choice: their soul melted: their courage was gone
decisions.reason: To melt is to lose all strength from fear (22:15; Joshua 2:11).
The word (ra'ah) here is not wickedness but disaster, the danger of the storm.
Readable names who went up and down.

records.source: יָח֣וֹגּוּ וְ֭יָנוּעוּ כַּשִּׁכּ֑וֹר וְכָל־חָ֝כְמָתָ֗ם תִּתְבַּלָּֽע׃
records.gloss: They reeled and staggered like the drunkard, and all their wisdom was swallowed up.
pieces: They lurched and swayed like someone drunk, and all their skill at sea came to nothing.

L.27: They reeled and staggered like a drunkard, and all their skill was swallowed up.

R.27: They swayed and stumbled like drunk people, and nothing they knew how to do could help them.

decisions.reason: The word (chokhmah) is used of a craftsman's or a sailor's skill (Exodus 31:3; Ezekiel 27:8). The sailors' seamanship was no use.

decisions.choice: was swallowed up: came to nothing
decisions.reason: The verb (bala') is to swallow; here their skill vanished, or was thrown into confusion.

records.source: וַיִּצְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם וּֽ֝מִמְּצֽוּקֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹצִיאֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And they cried out to YHWH in the distress [that was] to them, and from their troubles he brought them out.
pieces: In their distress they called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out from their troubles.

L.28: Then they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in their distress; and from their troubles {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out.

R.28: In their trouble they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them safely out from their suffering.

decisions.reason: As in verse 6; only the verb of rescue changes.
As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: brought them out: led them out of danger
decisions.reason: The verb (yatsa', causative) is the one used of bringing Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 20:2) and the prisoners out of the dark (verse 14).

decisions.choice: in their distress ... from their troubles
alternatives: they cried out ... in their trouble, and he ... them from their distress
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

records.source: יָקֵ֣ם סְ֭עָרָה לִדְמָמָ֑ה וַ֝יֶּחֱשׁ֗וּ גַּלֵּיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: He made stand [the] storm to a whisper, and their waves were still.
pieces: He turned the gale into a gentle breath, and the waves around them fell silent.

L.29: He made the storm into a whisper, and their waves were hushed.

R.29: He made the storm grow as quiet as a whisper, and the waves became calm.

decisions.reason: The word (demamah) is the hush that Elijah heard after the wind and the fire (1 Kings 19).
In the Gospels Jesus stills the wind and the sea with a word, and his disciples ask who this is whom even the wind and the sea obey (Mark 4:39-41).

decisions.choice: their waves: the waves around them
decisions.reason: "Their" may refer to the sailors (the waves that threatened them) or to the waters.

records.source: וַיִּשְׂמְח֥וּ כִֽי־יִשְׁתֹּ֑קוּ וַ֝יַּנְחֵ֗ם אֶל־מְח֥וֹז חֶפְצָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they rejoiced, for they were quiet, and he guided them to [the] harbor of their desire.
pieces: How glad they were when all grew still! And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them to the harbor they longed for.

L.30: And they rejoiced because they were quiet, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} guided them to the harbor of their desire.

R.30: The sailors were happy when everything was calm, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them safely to the port where they wanted to go.

decisions.choice: they were quiet: the waves, or the sailors, grew still
decisions.reason: "They" may be the waves of verse 29 or the sailors themselves, calm after their terror. Either way all was still.

decisions.choice: harbor: a haven by the shore
decisions.reason: The word (machoz) is found only here in the Bible. It is probably a harbor or a trading town on the coast.

decisions.choice: when all grew still (B); when everything was calm (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave open who or what was quiet (m1).

records.source: יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: Let them give thanks to YHWH [for] his loyal love, and his wonders to [the] children of humankind.
pieces: Let them give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love and for the wonders {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} works for humankind.

L.31: Let them give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [for] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love, and [for] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders to the children of humankind.

R.31: They should thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love and for the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does for people.

decisions.reason: As in verse 8, word for word.
As in verse 1.
As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: to the children of humankind: done for people
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: וִֽ֭ירֹמְמוּהוּ בִּקְהַל־עָ֑ם וּבְמוֹשַׁ֖ב זְקֵנִ֣ים יְהַלְלֽוּהוּ׃
records.gloss: And let them exalt him in [the] assembly of [the] people, and in [the] seat of [the] elders let them praise him.
pieces: Let them lift {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} high where the people gather and praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} where the elders sit in council.

L.32: And let them exalt {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the assembly of the people, and in the seat of the elders let them praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.32: Let them honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} when all the people meet together, and praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in front of the leaders.

decisions.choice: the seat of the elders: the town council
decisions.reason: The elders sat together, often at the town gate, to judge and to decide (Ruth 4:2). Thanks for a rescue was given in public, before everyone (22:23, 26).
The verb (rum, intensive) is to raise up, here to honor God with praise.

records.source: יָשֵׂ֣ם נְהָר֣וֹת לְמִדְבָּ֑ר וּמֹצָ֥אֵי מַ֝֗יִם לְצִמָּאֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: He makes rivers into a wilderness, and springs of water into thirsty ground,
pieces: He can dry up rivers until they are desert and turn springs of water into parched land,

L.33: He makes rivers into a wilderness, and springs of water into thirsty ground,

R.33: God can make rivers dry up and become desert. He can turn springs of water into dry, thirsty ground.

decisions.choice: the second half: God turns things around
decisions.reason: The refrains stop here. Verses 33-43 praise God who reverses things: he dries up rivers and makes the desert flow (33-35), brings the hungry to settle (36-38), and humbles the proud while lifting the needy (39-41), in the manner of the wisdom books (Job 12:21-24).

decisions.choice: what God does at any time
decisions.reason: The Hebrew mixes present and past verb forms in verses 33-41. They describe what God does again and again, so all levels use the present.
The list continues into verse 34, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
Readable names God at the start of the new section.

records.source: אֶ֣רֶץ פְּ֭רִי לִמְלֵחָ֑ה מֵ֝רָעַ֗ת יֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: a land of fruit into a salt waste, because of [the] evil of those who dwell in it.
pieces: and rich farmland into a salt flat, for the evil done by those who live there.

L.34: a land of fruit into a salt waste, because of the evil of those who dwell in it.

R.34: He can turn rich farmland into useless, salty ground, because the people who live there are evil.

decisions.choice: a salt waste: the land around Sodom
decisions.reason: The well-watered plain of Sodom became a wasteland when God judged its people (Genesis 13:10; 19:24-25). Salt land grows nothing (Job 39:6).

decisions.choice: judgment on the land for its people's evil
decisions.reason: The land suffers for the wickedness of those who live on it (Genesis 3:17-18).

records.source: יָשֵׂ֣ם מִ֭דְבָּר לַֽאֲגַם־מַ֑יִם וְאֶ֥רֶץ צִ֝יָּ֗ה לְמֹצָ֥אֵי מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: He makes a wilderness into a pool of water, and a land of dryness into springs of water.
pieces: He makes the desert a pool of water and dry country into bubbling springs.

L.35: He makes a wilderness into a pool of water, and a land of dryness into springs of water.

R.35: He can also turn a desert into a lake, and dry land into springs of water.

decisions.choice: a wilderness into a pool: Isaiah 41:18
decisions.reason: God promised the exiles, "I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water" (Isaiah 41:18). This verse is the reverse of verse 33.

records.source: וַיּ֣וֹשֶׁב שָׁ֣ם רְעֵבִ֑ים וַ֝יְכוֹנְנ֗וּ עִ֣יר מוֹשָֽׁב׃
records.gloss: And he makes dwell there [the] hungry, and they establish a city of dwelling.
pieces: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} settles the hungry, and they build a town to live in.

L.36: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes the hungry dwell there, and they establish a city [to] dwell [in].

R.36: He brings hungry people to live there, and they build a town for their homes.

decisions.choice: a city of dwelling: the town the lost could not find
decisions.reason: The same words as in verses 4 and 7. The hungry who wandered (verse 5) now build the town they looked for.

records.source: וַיִּזְרְע֣וּ שָׂ֭דוֹת וַיִּטְּע֣וּ כְרָמִ֑ים וַ֝יַּעֲשׂ֗וּ פְּרִ֣י תְבֽוּאָה׃
records.gloss: And they sow fields and plant vineyards, and they make fruit of produce.
pieces: They seed the fields and plant vines, and gather a rich harvest.

L.37: And they sow fields and plant vineyards, and they make fruit [of] harvest.

R.37: They plant crops in the fields and grapevines in vineyards, and they gather a big harvest.

decisions.choice: fruit of produce: a full harvest
decisions.reason: The two words for crops together mean a rich yield (Leviticus 25:19).

records.source: וַיְבָרֲכֵ֣ם וַיִּרְבּ֣וּ מְאֹ֑ד וּ֝בְהֶמְתָּ֗ם לֹ֣א יַמְעִֽיט׃
records.gloss: And he blesses them, and they multiply exceedingly, and their cattle he does not make few.
pieces: He blesses them, and their numbers grow and grow; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not let their herds dwindle.

L.38: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blesses them, and they multiply greatly, and their cattle {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not let decrease.

R.38: He blesses them, and their families grow larger and larger. He keeps their herds of cattle from getting smaller.

decisions.reason: Blessing and growing in number go together from the first blessing on (Genesis 1:28; 12:2).
The word (behemah) is domestic animals in general, the wealth of a farming family.

records.source: וַיִּמְעֲט֥וּ וַיָּשֹׁ֑חוּ מֵעֹ֖צֶר רָעָ֣ה וְיָגֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And they become few and are bowed down from [the] oppression of evil and sorrow.
pieces: Then they dwindle and are brought down by cruel rule, disaster and grief.

L.39: Then they become few and are bowed down through oppression, evil, and sorrow.

R.39: But then they become fewer, and they are crushed by cruel treatment, by trouble and by sorrow.

decisions.choice: they become few: a turn of fortune
alternatives: the proud of verse 40 are made few
decisions.reason: The verse turns from blessing to loss. It may describe the same people when oppressors come, whom God then judges (verse 40); or it may already describe the proud who are brought down. Either way God reverses their fortunes.
The word ('otser) is pressure or restraint; with "evil" (ra'ah, disaster) it is harsh oppression.

records.source: שֹׁפֵ֣ךְ בּ֭וּז עַל־נְדִיבִ֑ים וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם בְּתֹ֣הוּ לֹא־דָֽרֶךְ׃
records.gloss: [He is] pouring out contempt on nobles, and he makes them wander in a wasteland [with] no way.
pieces: He heaps scorn on the powerful and leaves them lost in a wasteland without a road.

L.40: [He is] pouring contempt on nobles, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes them wander in a wasteland [with] no way.

R.40: He shames proud rulers and makes them wander lost in a desert where there is no road.

decisions.reason: Both halves of this verse are found in Job's praise of God's power: "he pours contempt on nobles" (Job 12:21) and "makes them wander in a wasteland with no way" (Job 12:24).
The word (tohu) is the formless emptiness of Genesis 1:2. The proud end up like the lost travelers of verse 4.

records.source: וַיְשַׂגֵּ֣ב אֶבְי֣וֹן מֵע֑וֹנִי וַיָּ֥שֶׂם כַּ֝צֹּ֗אן מִשְׁפָּחֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And he sets on high [the] needy from affliction, and makes like the flock families.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raises the needy from their misery and makes their families grow like flocks of sheep.

L.41: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sets the needy on high, out of affliction, and makes [their] families like a flock.

R.41: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lifts poor people out of their trouble and gives them big families, as many as a flock of sheep.

decisions.choice: sets on high: lifts to safety
decisions.reason: The verb (sagav) is to set high out of reach, safe from harm (20:2; 91:14).

decisions.choice: families like the flock: many children
decisions.reason: A flock grows quickly; so their families grow large (Job 21:11).

records.source: יִרְא֣וּ יְשָׁרִ֣ים וְיִשְׂמָ֑חוּ וְכָל־עַ֝וְלָ֗ה קָ֣פְצָה פִּֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: [The] upright see and rejoice, and all injustice shuts its mouth.
pieces: Those who live upright lives look on with joy, and all wickedness has nothing more to say.

L.42: The upright see [it] and rejoice, and all injustice shuts its mouth.

R.42: Honest people see this and are happy, and wicked people have nothing left to say.

decisions.reason: The same words are found in Job 5:16: when God lifts the poor, injustice has no answer.
Injustice is pictured as a person who can only fall silent.
Readable speaks of the people rather than the quality.

records.source: מִי־חָכָ֥ם וְיִשְׁמָר־אֵ֑לֶּה וְ֝יִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֗וּ חַֽסְדֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Who [is] wise, and let him keep these, and let them consider [the] loyal loves of YHWH.
pieces: Whoever is wise should mark these things and ponder the loyal love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has shown again and again.

L.43: Whoever [is] wise, let {{gender:them|him}} keep these [things], and let them consider the acts of loyal love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.43: Anyone who is wise will take all this to heart and think about the many times {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has shown {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love.

decisions.choice: who is wise: whoever is wise
decisions.reason: The question invites anyone who is wise to take this to heart. The verb changes from singular ("let him keep") to plural ("let them consider"): each wise person, and all of them.
As in verse 1. The plural (chasde) means God's many acts of loyal love, like the four rescues in this psalm.
The psalm ends like a wisdom book, calling the wise to understand the LORD's ways (Proverbs 1:5-6). The book of Hosea ends in the same way.
The Hebrew speaks of any wise person as "he"; the default says "them", with "him" as the alternative.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
